notes: data/lawsuits.json is kept current by the weekly automated run (scripts/update_tracker.py), which only searches a ~7-10 day window each time. Because the repo launched empty, that narrow window meant the first scheduled run could only find lawsuits filed in roughly the prior week (Jimison) and structurally could not backfill older cases. This 2026-08-04 batch is a manual backfill research pass covering several notable Flock-related suits, added with verified:false pending human review. Aggregate 'as of' figures from external trackers should be checked against, not summed with, this list.

lawsuits.allegation_summary: Filed by ACLU-WV, the Haslam Law Firm, and Glazer, Saad, Anderson immediately after Huntington City Council approved a $2.1 million Flock Safety ALPR contract in a contentious 6-4 vote; alleges the city failed to follow required procedures in awarding the contract, including improper authorization for a private company to use public property for the cameras.
lawsuits.status_detail: Lawsuit filed July 14, 2026, same day as the council vote; ACLU-WV legal director indicated additional legal claims could follow beyond the procedural challenge.

lawsuits.allegation_summary: Aurora police used a Flock-style ALPR hot-list alert that misread a stolen motorcycle plate as matching Gilliam and her family's SUV; officers held Gilliam and four children, including minors, at gunpoint and handcuffed them face-down on pavement during a botched stolen-vehicle stop.
lawsuits.status_detail: City of Aurora settled with Gilliam for $1.9 million (settlement reported 2024, following a 2021 filing over a 2020 incident). Court/case number not confirmed from the sourcing reviewed for this entry. Most contemporaneous 2020-2021 coverage described the system only as a license-plate-reader hot-list match without naming the vendor; later retrospective reporting on Flock misuse (e.g. CNN, 2026) cites this case as a Flock example -- flagged for maintainer verification of the ALPR vendor.

lawsuits.case_name: Upchurch v. City of Toledo, et al.
lawsuits.court: U.S. District Court for the Northern District of Ohio
lawsuits.allegation_summary: A Flock camera misread the "7" on Upchurch's license plate as a "2", falsely matching it to a stolen-vehicle hot list; Toledo police stopped Upchurch, and an officer released a police K9 that bit and injured him even though the truck was correctly his own, non-stolen vehicle.
lawsuits.status_detail: Federal case Upchurch v. City of Toledo, et al., No. 3:25-cv-00711 (N.D. Ohio). Reported settlement of $35,000 with the city and an officer (2025).

lawsuits.court: First Judicial District Court, Rio Arriba County, NM (case number not confirmed)
plaintiffs: Unnamed minor sister (12, identified in reporting by initials D.D.)
lawsuits.allegation_summary: A Flock Safety camera misread the plaintiffs' license plate (ending in 2, misread as 7) as matching a stolen vehicle; Española police stopped, handcuffed, and detained Gonzales and her 12-year-old sister at gunpoint before discovering the error.
lawsuits.status_detail: Filed January 3 (year approximate, ~2024) in New Mexico state district court. Resolution not confirmed from the sourcing reviewed.

lawsuits.allegation_summary: A Flock camera misread the letter "H" on Burkleo's license plate as "M" (a dirt-obscured character), falsely flagging his car as matching a wanted vehicle; Atherton police stopped Burkleo at gunpoint and ordered him to the ground before discovering the error.
lawsuits.status_detail: Settled with the town and involved officers for $45,000 per news reporting; exact filing date, court, and case number not confirmed from sourcing reviewed. Atherton Police Department publicly denied wrongdoing.

lawsuits.court: U.S. District Court for the District of New Mexico
lawsuits.allegation_summary: Then-17-year-old honor-roll student Adam Pacheco was pulled over and handcuffed at gunpoint by a New Mexico State Police officer based on inaccurate information tied to a Flock Safety camera alert while driving home from Pojoaque High School.
lawsuits.status_detail: Federal case Pacheco v. City of Española, No. 1:23-cv-00593 (D.N.M.). Reporting indicates New Mexico State Police paid $200,000 in connection with the case; city-side resolution not separately confirmed from sourcing reviewed.

lawsuits.case_name: Moore v. City and County of San Francisco
lawsuits.court: U.S. District Court for the Northern District of California
defendants: City and County of San Francisco
lawsuits.allegation_summary: Proposed class action alleging that San Francisco police's network of roughly 500 Flock Safety ALPR cameras constitutes "warrantless and unreasonable" mass surveillance in violation of the Fourth Amendment.
lawsuits.status_detail: Filed as a proposed class action against the City and County of San Francisco and SFPD in N.D. Cal.; exact filing date and case number not confirmed from sourcing reviewed. NOTE FOR MAINTAINER: this is the closest verified match found for a suit naming the City/County of San Francisco itself -- I could not confirm a case captioned "Green v. City and County of San Francisco" as requested; please check the exact caption against the source article, or supply a link if you have one, before treating this as the correct entry.

lawsuits.case_name: Hofer v. County of Contra Costa, et al.
lawsuits.court: Likely U.S. District Court for the Northern District of California (venue not confirmed from sourcing reviewed)
defendants: Three Contra Costa County Sheriff's deputies (named individually; names not confirmed from sourcing reviewed)
lawsuits.allegation_summary: An automated license plate reader flagged Hofer's rental car as stolen based on a "stale" database entry -- the vehicle had already been recovered and returned to circulation -- and Contra Costa County Sheriff's deputies conducted a high-risk "felony stop" at gunpoint on Hofer and his brother without verifying the alert.
lawsuits.status_detail: Federal civil-rights suit filed December 2018 against three Contra Costa County Sheriff's deputies (individual civil rights, warrantless search, and excessive force claims) over a November 25, 2018 stop. Contra Costa County settled for $49,500 (paid to Hofer in an August payout). ALPR vendor not confirmed as Flock Safety in sourcing reviewed -- Flock was newly founded in 2017 and this stop predates its market dominance; flagged for maintainer verification before treating as a confirmed Flock case.

lawsuits.court: U.S. District Court for the Northern District of California
plaintiffs: Javorsky (lead plaintiff; additional plaintiffs not fully confirmed from sourcing)
lawsuits.allegation_summary: Federal suit against Flock Safety alleging its ALPR network enables unauthorized mass collection and sharing of license-plate data, framed around privacy and data-broker-style claims; part of a wave of 2026 California suits over Flock sharing plate data with out-of-state and federal agencies.
lawsuits.status_detail: Docket No. 3:26-cv-02382 (N.D. Cal.). Related to (but may be distinct from) a separate Gibbs Mura / Milberg PLLC class action filed February 26, 2026 in San Francisco Superior Court against Flock Safety over California ALPR Privacy Act violations (alleged sharing of SFPD's Flock data with out-of-state/federal agencies 1.6M+ times). Maintainer should confirm whether these are the same suit or two separate ones before treating this entry as fully resolved. Not on the user's original list -- added because it's a well-documented, on-topic suit found during this backfill pass.

lawsuits.allegation_summary: Wichita resident and privacy activist Mason Grimmett alleges the city's roughly 200 Flock Safety ALPR cameras, capturing about 900,000 vehicle photos monthly, constitute a warrantless dragnet surveillance program that violates the privacy protections of Section 15 of the Kansas Constitution Bill of Rights. The suit seeks a declaration that the program is unconstitutional and an order requiring removal of the cameras.
lawsuits.status_detail: Petition filed July 30, 2026 in Sedgwick County District Court by the Kansas Justice Institute; cites Wichita's own data showing 904,603 license plate searches in a single month (June 26-July 27, 2026) and prior officer misuse cases (e.g., former Kechi Police lieutenant convicted of using Flock data to stalk his estranged wife).
